note: Self-contained oracle case (stdlib only, not replay-driven), proven directly with effect='canary_exec'. Held out: written after the compact profile and the oracle were frozen. The app is an original multi-package document suite; the vulnerability pattern (request input reaching a command-execution sink) follows the class analog below. No upstream repo/commit applies.

real_world_analog.fix: GitLab upgraded the bundled ExifTool past 12.23 so DjVu metadata is no longer evaluated; the general fix for the class is to never pass request input to a shell (argument vector without a shell, plus strict allow-listing). The fixed tree does the same with an original argv call plus a plain-name check.
real_world_analog.summary: Remote code execution in GitLab CE/EE: an unauthenticated image upload reached ExifTool, whose DjVu handler evaluated attacker metadata and executed commands (root cause CVE-2021-22204). The pattern is request input reaching a command-execution sink.
real_world_analog.verification: CVE number and summary confirmed via web search on 2026-10-31; the app in this case is original code written for Exhibit A, not GitLab or ExifTool.
